web-guide-idea-29.audience: Adults looking for an attentive, everyday conversation.
web-guide-idea-29.offer: Offer a clearly bounded listening appointment where one person gets your full attention. This is adult companionship, not counselling, diagnosis or crisis care.
web-guide-idea-29.steps.0: Agree the session length and conversational boundaries.
web-guide-idea-29.steps.1: Let the other person choose what to talk about and listen without rushing to advice.
web-guide-idea-29.steps.2: Close gently at the agreed time and ask what felt useful.
web-guide-idea-29.equipment: A phone with a camera, earphones, reliable internet and a private, quiet room. A laptop is optional; nobody else should be listening off-camera.
web-guide-idea-29.returnReason: People may return because you remember their preferences and give them a respectful space. Keep professional boundaries and avoid creating pressure or dependence.
web-guide-idea-29.promotion: Describe your language, availability and listening style. Never share someone’s story as a promotional example without their explicit permission.
